The SYSCALL is unlink (syscall 87) deleting ".auditf.service.swp", the vim swap file, in /etc/systemd/system/.

This is a root-owned process, initiated by an audit user (auid=john) who escalated to root, editing a systemd service unit with an unusual name ("auditf" resembling a masquerading service) in a persistence-relevant directory. Deleting the swap file is a routine vim action on normal exit, so the deletion alone is not malicious. However, creating/editing a systemd service as root under an obscure name is a plausible persistence pattern.
